name: Heal from a harmful effect
summary: A harmful effect that slows, poisons or burns other units heals this one instead. Most often the unit uses up a status that builds on it (stacks of a slowing charge become repairs), or regains health while standing in a hazard field that hurts everyone else; rarer versions drink one kind of shot while a key is held, or turn all damage into healing for a few seconds. The enemy's tool for that effect becomes a gift, so they must switch weapons or targets. Every version keeps a limit: an overload stage that still hurts (the Tempest Sphere's plating can't keep up with Overflow), a cap on the healing, other damage that hits normally, or a field it must stay in. The levers are which effect it feeds on, how much each dose heals and what still hurts it.
counterplay: Stop feeding it: keep your slowing or charging weapons and fields off it and switch to plain damage it can't use; cannon hits strike the Tempest Sphere at full strength.

Push it past the limit: stack the status fast enough to reach the overload stage, which hurts the Sphere faster than its plating repairs it; in Tempest Rising some shots also destroy any vehicle caught in Overflow outright.
Fight it away from its field: a unit that heals in a hazard zone (mutants in Tiberium, Veti machines in Tempest fields) is an ordinary target once it is lured or pushed out.

Wait out the window: against a version that turns all damage into healing for a few seconds (Abaddon's Borrowed Time), hold fire until it ends, or take it from healthy to dead in one blow so the automatic trigger never fires.
Use the attacks it can't take in: PSI Magnet drinks mainly energy shots, so physical projectiles and close attacks get through.

other_examples.unit: Mutants and cyborgs (the Forgotten and Nod)
other_examples.note: Tiberium has poisoned the Forgotten, and its veins damage nearby units, vehicles and buildings, yet every mutant unit, such as the Ghostalker and the mutant hijacker, regains health while standing in Tiberium; the hijacker only while he is not inside a stolen vehicle. Nod's cyborgs, made from mutated humans, heal there too, so Tiberium fields are friendly ground for them.

sources.title: Command & Conquer: Tiberian Sun manual (transcript), Command & Conquer Wiki
sources.note: Copies the Tiberian Sun manual: the Forgotten, the Tiberium veins and the Ghostalker, mutant hijacker and cyborg entries.

other_examples.unit: Mastermind (Scrin), with the Cultists of Traveler-59 (Kane's Wrath)
other_examples.note: These Scrin infantry heal while standing in a Tiberium field. GDI's Zone Troopers, by contrast, are only spared the field's harm and lose no health in it, which shows the line between immunity and feeding.

sources.title: Zone trooper (Tiberium Wars), Command & Conquer Wiki

other_examples.unit: Symbiotic Restoration (Veti vehicles and aircraft, Engine Tuning doctrine)
other_examples.note: Ground vehicles in a Tempest field build up Charge that slows their movement and fire, and too much of it tips into Overflow. A doctrine the Veti can buy makes their vehicles and aircraft fully immune to Charge and has them slowly repair themselves while inside a Tempest field. The Tempest Rising notes keep it off the units because it reaches the whole class.

His ultimate makes every hit he takes heal him instead of hurting him for a few seconds, and strips most debuffs as it starts. If it is off cooldown it also starts by itself when his health drops low, though not when one hit takes more than the health he has left, nor against instant kills, and Break stops the automatic start. Anti-heal effects can still shrink the healing.

other_examples.unit: Poison Heal (ability of Breloom, Gliscor and Shroomish)
other_examples.note: A Pokémon with this ability regains health each turn while it is poisoned rather than losing health, so a poison that wears other Pokémon down keeps it topped up instead. The in-game text in each generation says the same.

sources.title: Poison Heal (ability), Pokémon Database
sources.note: Lists the in-game description of the ability from each generation.

shooter_analogues.note: Phoenix's fire abilities, a wall of flame and a thrown firebomb, burn enemies, but when he touches his own flames they heal him over time instead, up to a set amount per ability. Since a later patch the heal keeps running after he leaves the fire.

sources.title: Passive Effects (reached through Heating Up), VALORANT Wiki

shooter_analogues.note: Their down special raises a psychic field for as long as the button is held. Certain projectiles, mostly energy attacks rather than physical objects, are soaked up by it and heal the user instead of hurting him. The two versions differ in size, speed, placement and how much they heal.

player_translation.summary: The enemy's slowing or poisoning tool heals you instead. You wade into their hazard fields and invite their status weapons, turning what would cripple another unit into repairs, until the dose gets so heavy that it overloads and hurts you anyway.
as_user: You go where others can't: through the enemy's slowing fields or into their charge-weapon fire, repairing as the status builds on you.
You watch your own meter: the status stacks show on your HUD, and you back off before they reach the overload stage, which still hurts, as Overflow does to the Tempest Sphere.
Home-field versions make you a defender of hazard zones: fight inside the field and you mend; step out and you are ordinary.
Against a team that relies on that status you are a counter-pick; against plain damage you are just a unit with no extra protection.
as_target: Your status weapon visibly heals it (green sparks instead of the usual effect, and a heal number), so you learn quickly to switch to plain damage.
Or pile on together: several sources stacking the status at once push it into the overload stage, where it loses more than it mends.
Lure it out of its field before you fight it, and keep your own hazards away from it.
teammates: Its team fights inside hazard zones or lays fields, letting it hold ground the enemy cannot.
The enemy team needs a plan: send plain-damage units against it, or coordinate a burst of the status to overload it.
A friendly field-layer and this unit make a pair, if friendly fields are allowed to heal it (see open questions).
controls: None for the base pattern: it is passive and spends no counted key.
The absorb-shots variant holds a field on Q while the key is held, one counted key; the borrowed-time variant is a key with a long cooldown that may also start by itself at low health.
feedback: The status looks different on this unit (gold or green sparks instead of the usual effect), so enemies see that it is being eaten, not suffered.
A green tick rises on its health bar each time a dose turns into repairs.
An overload warning (flashing stacks and a crackle) as it nears the stage that hurts it, readable by both sides.
Field versions tint the unit while it stands in a field that heals it.
changes_from_rts: In Tempest Rising the plating is one perk on one unit among many, and the sources describe no cue for its repairs; a player must see each dose eaten and each repair, and the enemy must see that their weapon feeds it.

The pattern needs a status to feed on: a slowing charge, poison or burning that other units fear. Without one in Shamble Frontlines it does nothing, so a card with it should face enemies that use such a status.
The overload stage must stay: RTS players seldom push a single unit into Overflow on purpose, but shooter players will, and it is the counterplay that keeps the pattern fair.
Home-field versions need fields where the fights happen: Tiberium and Tempest spread across RTS maps, while in a shooter the fields come from abilities or set map zones.

team_play.notes: It punishes a team built around one status: they must change picks or coordinate an overload burst. Its own team holds hazard zones with it or lures enemies into fields where it heals and they suffer.

notes: Needs a status-effect system with stacks the unit can use up, and a clear rule for the overload stage.
Home-field versions need zones that know which units they heal and which they hurt.
The feedback is new work: art and sound that show a status turning into healing rather than harm.

It shuts out one family of weapons: a team built on that status can be left with no answer, so keep each dose's repair modest (the Sphere regains a modest share of its health per use) and the overload stage dangerous.
In a large home field it can become very hard to kill; keep fields small or the healing slow.
The borrowed-time variant is a strong panic button; it needs a long cooldown and a way to beat the automatic start.
Players expect their status to hurt; a unit that heals from it surprises them unless its look changes clearly.
The overload stage must be just as readable, or attackers never learn the counterplay.

variants.name: Feed on a status
variants.summary: Stacks of a slowing or weakening status that enemy weapons or fields put on it are used up to repair it; past an overload point the status still hurts it.

variants.name: Thrive on poison
variants.summary: While a poison or other lingering damage is on it, it regains health instead of losing it, for as long as the effect lasts.

counters.why: Weapons that poison or burn it over time heal it for as long as the effect lasts.

variants.name: Home field
variants.summary: It heals while standing in a hazard field that hurts or slows everyone else, whether the map, the enemy or its own side made the field.
variants.seen_in: Tiberian Sun mutants and cyborgs, Tiberium Wars Scrin infantry (Tiberium); Tempest Rising Veti machines with Engine Tuning (Tempest fields)

adds_weaknesses.why: Away from a hazard field it gets no healing at all, so enemies choose to fight it elsewhere.

variants.name: Healed by its own fire
variants.summary: Its own hazard, such as a fire wall or a firebomb, burns enemies but heals it, so dropping one at its feet is a heal and a barrier at once.

variants.name: Drink one kind of shot
variants.summary: While a key is held, a field soaks up one kind of enemy shot, such as energy bolts, and turns it into health; everything else gets through.
variants.seen_in: Super Smash Bros. Ness and Lucas (PSI Magnet)

adds_weaknesses.why: It drinks only one kind of shot and only while the key is held; every other attack goes through.

counters.why: Energy shots fired into its field heal it instead of hurting it.

variants.name: Borrowed time
variants.summary: For a few seconds every hit heals it instead of hurting it; it starts on a key or by itself when health drops low, then waits out a long cooldown.

adds_strengths.why: For a few seconds every hit heals it, and the window can start by itself to save it at low health.

adds_weaknesses.why: Outside its short window it has no protection, and one blow that takes it from healthy to dead beats the automatic start.

countered_by.why: One big charged shot can take it from healthy to dead before the automatic start fires.

adds_strengths.why: Enemy weapons or fields that would slow or poison it repair it instead.

adds_weaknesses.why: The feeding has a limit: an overload stage or a heavy dose still hurts it, and other damage hits it normally.

counters.why: A lone enemy whose weapon slows or charges it only feeds it repairs, as Tempest Charge does for the Tempest Sphere.
Hazard fields meant to hurt or slow it become places where it heals, as Tiberium does for mutants.

countered_by.why: Several enemies stacking the status at once push it into the overload stage, which hurts it faster than it repairs, as Overflow does the Sphere.

open_questions: Which status in Shamble Frontlines would it feed on: an electric charge that slows vehicles, poison, burning? The pattern only matters if enough enemy cards use that status.

Should feeding also cancel the status's slowdown, or does the unit still suffer the slow while it repairs? The sources say the Tempest Sphere's plating uses the Charge up, but not whether the slow bites first.

May a teammate's field or status heal it, as the Veti doctrine heals its own side's machines in Tempest fields, or only the enemy's? Friendly feeding makes a strong pair with a teammate who lays fields.
Should the borrowed-time variant, which turns all damage into healing, stay here or move to become-invulnerable?

shooter_fit.reason: Gives fresh counterplay (switch weapons or overload it) and has a shooter precedent in Valorant's Phoenix, but it only works where the game has a status or field that other units fear, and attackers need clear feedback that their slow feeds it.
